Computes the blocking parameters for a m x k times k x n matrix product 


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{引数}
\mbox{\texttt{ in,out}}  & {\em k} & Input\+: the third dimension of the product. Output\+: the blocking size along the same dimension. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in,out}}  & {\em m} & Input\+: the number of rows of the left hand side. Output\+: the blocking size along the same dimension. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in,out}}  & {\em n} & Input\+: the number of columns of the right hand side. Output\+: the blocking size along the same dimension.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
Given a m x k times k x n matrix product of scalar types {\ttfamily Lhs\+Scalar} and {\ttfamily Rhs\+Scalar}, this function computes the blocking size parameters along the respective dimensions for matrix products and related algorithms.

The blocking size parameters may be evaluated\+:
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item either by a heuristic based on cache sizes;
\item or using fixed prescribed values (for testing purposes).
\end{DoxyItemize}

Symm packing is related to packing of symmetric adjoint blocks, as expected the packing leaves the diagonal real, whatever is below it is copied from the respective upper diagonal element and conjugated. There\textquotesingle{}s no Panel\+Mode available for symm packing.

Packing in general is supposed to leave the lhs block and the rhs block easy to be read by gemm using its respective rank-\/update instructions. The float32/64 versions are different because at this moment the size of the accumulator is fixed at 512-\/bits so you can\textquotesingle{}t have a 4x4 accumulator of 64-\/bit elements.

As mentioned earlier Matrix\+Product breaks complex numbers into a real vector and a complex vector so packing has to take that into account, at the moment, we run pack the real part and then the imaginary part, this is the main reason why packing for complex is broken down into several different parts, also the reason why we endup having a float32/64 and complex float32/64 version. \Hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a1dea9d8b6c751ae8d2a60b8760dcd441_a1dea9d8b6c751ae8d2a60b8760dcd441}\index{Eigen::internal@{Eigen::internal}!GetMarketLine@{GetMarketLine}}

Generalized Minimal Residual Algorithm based on the Arnoldi algorithm implemented with Householder reflections.

Parameters\+: 
\begin{DoxyParams}{引数}
{\em mat} & matrix of linear system of equations \\
\hline
{\em rhs} & right hand side vector of linear system of equations \\
\hline
{\em x} & on input\+: initial guess, on output\+: solution \\
\hline
{\em precond} & preconditioner used \\
\hline
{\em iters} & on input\+: maximum number of iterations to perform on output\+: number of iterations performed \\
\hline
{\em restart} & number of iterations for a restart \\
\hline
{\em tol\+\_\+error} & on input\+: relative residual tolerance on output\+: residuum achieved\\

This routine completes the computation of {\ttfamily fT}, denoting a matrix function applied to the triangular matrix {\ttfamily T}. This routine computes the matrix function applied to the block diagonal part of {\ttfamily T} (which should be upper triangular), with the blocking given by {\ttfamily block\+Start} and {\ttfamily cluster\+Size}. The partition satisfies the following two properties\+: \hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a9291a6ab4fe0ad1346049a8f2feddeaa_autotoc_md220}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Any eigenvalue in a certain cluster is at most matrix\+\_\+function\+\_\+separation() away from another eigenvalue}{Any eigenvalue in a certain cluster is at most matrix\+\_\+function\+\_\+separation() away from another eigenvalue}}\label{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a9291a6ab4fe0ad1346049a8f2feddeaa_autotoc_md220}
in the same cluster. \hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a9291a6ab4fe0ad1346049a8f2feddeaa_autotoc_md221}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{The distance between two eigenvalues in different clusters is more than matrix\+\_\+function\+\_\+separation().}{The distance between two eigenvalues in different clusters is more than matrix\+\_\+function\+\_\+separation().}}\label{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a9291a6ab4fe0ad1346049a8f2feddeaa_autotoc_md221}

\doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_solve}{Solve} a triangular Sylvester equation AX + XB = C 


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{引数}
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em A} & the matrix A; should be square and upper triangular \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em B} & the matrix B; should be square and upper triangular \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em C} & the matrix C; should have correct size.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
\begin{DoxyReturn}{戻り値}
the solution X.
\end{DoxyReturn}
If A is m-\/by-\/m and B is n-\/by-\/n, then both C and X are m-\/by-\/n. The (i,j)-\/th component of the Sylvester equation is   \[ 
    \sum_{k=i}^m A_{ik} X_{kj} + \sum_{k=1}^j X_{ik} B_{kj} = C_{ij}. 
\] This can be re-\/arranged to yield\+:    \[ 
    X_{ij} = \frac{1}{A_{ii} + B_{jj}} \Bigl( C_{ij}
    - \sum_{k=i+1}^m A_{ik} X_{kj} - \sum_{k=1}^{j-1} X_{ik} B_{kj} \Bigr).
\] It is assumed that A and B are such that the numerator is never zero (otherwise the Sylvester equation does not have a unique solution). In that case, these equations can be evaluated in the order $ i=m,\ldots,1 $ and $ j=1,\ldots,n $. \Hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_a1cb8d312c017f94570a52317fd1ece5f_a1cb8d312c017f94570a52317fd1ece5f}\index{Eigen::internal@{Eigen::internal}!matrix\_log\_compute\_2x2@{matrix\_log\_compute\_2x2}}

void Eigen\+::internal\+::pseudo\+\_\+inverse (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const CMatrix \&}]{C}{, }\item[{CINVMatrix \&}]{CINV}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Compute the pseudo inverse of the non-\/square matrix C such that $ CINV = (C * C^T)^{-1} * C $ based on a conjugate gradient method.

Computes the integer square root \begin{DoxyRemark}{注釈}
The calculation is performed using an algorithm which iterates through each binary digit of the result and tests whether setting that digit to 1 would cause the square of the value to be greater than the argument value. The algorithm is described in detail here\+: \href{http://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/AppNotes/91040a.pdf}{\texttt{ http\+://ww1.\+microchip.\+com/downloads/en/\+App\+Notes/91040a.\+pdf}} .    
\end{DoxyRemark}

Computes the integer square root \begin{DoxyRemark}{注釈}
The calculation is performed using an algorithm which iterates through each binary digit of the result and tests whether setting that digit to 1 would cause the square of the value to be greater than the argument value. Computing a decomposition of a dense matrix takes O(n\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}3) operations, while this method estimates the condition number quickly and reliably in O(n\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}2) operations.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{戻り値}
an estimate of the reciprocal condition number (1 / (\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}matrix\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1 \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}inv(matrix)\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1)) of matrix, given \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}matrix\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1 and its decomposition. Supports the following decompositions\+: \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_full_piv_l_u}{Full\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_partial_piv_l_u}{Partial\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_d_l_t}{LDLT}, and \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_l_t}{LLT}.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxySeeAlso}{参照}
\doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_full_piv_l_u}{Full\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_partial_piv_l_u}{Partial\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_d_l_t}{LDLT}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_l_t}{LLT}. 
\end{DoxySeeAlso}
\Hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_aa3f5b3cfa34df750994a247d4823aa51_aa3f5b3cfa34df750994a247d4823aa51}\index{Eigen::internal@{Eigen::internal}!rcond\_invmatrix\_L1\_norm\_estimate@{rcond\_invmatrix\_L1\_norm\_estimate}}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{rcond\_invmatrix\_L1\_norm\_estimate()}{rcond\_invmatrix\_L1\_norm\_estimate()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_aa3f5b3cfa34df750994a247d4823aa51_aa3f5b3cfa34df750994a247d4823aa51} 
template$<$typename Decomposition $>$ \\
Decomposition\+::\+Real\+Scalar Eigen\+::internal\+::rcond\+\_\+invmatrix\+\_\+\+L1\+\_\+norm\+\_\+estimate (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const Decomposition \&}]{dec}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

\begin{DoxyReturn}{戻り値}
an estimate of \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}inv(matrix)\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1 given a decomposition of {\itshape matrix} that implements .solve() and .\doxylink{adjoint_8cpp_a7333648f53414b05be9e4fd2f009fc22_a7333648f53414b05be9e4fd2f009fc22}{adjoint()}.solve() methods.
\end{DoxyReturn}
This function implements Algorithms 4.\+1 and 5.\+1 from \href{http://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/~higham/narep/narep135.pdf}{\texttt{ http\+://www.\+maths.\+manchester.\+ac.\+uk/\texorpdfstring{$\sim$}{\string~}higham/narep/narep135.\+pdf}} which also forms the basis for the condition number estimators in LAPACK. Since at most 10 calls to the solve method of dec are performed, the total cost is O(dims\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}2), as opposed to O(dims\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}3) needed to compute the inverse matrix explicitly.

The most common usage is in estimating the condition number \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}matrix\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1 \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}inv(matrix)\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1. The first term \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}matrix\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\+\_\+1 can be computed directly in O(n\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}2) operations.

Supports the following decompositions\+: \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_full_piv_l_u}{Full\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_partial_piv_l_u}{Partial\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_d_l_t}{LDLT}, and \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_l_t}{LLT}.

\begin{DoxySeeAlso}{参照}
\doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_full_piv_l_u}{Full\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_partial_piv_l_u}{Partial\+Piv\+LU}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_d_l_t}{LDLT}, \doxylink{class_eigen_1_1_l_l_t}{LLT}. 
\end{DoxySeeAlso}

Panel\+Mode Packing might be called several times before being multiplied by \doxylink{struct_eigen_1_1internal_1_1gebp__kernel}{gebp\+\_\+kernel}, this happens because on special occasions it fills part of block with other parts of the matrix. Two variables control how Panel\+Mode should behave\+: offset and stride. The idea is that those variables represent whatever is going to be the real offset and stride in the future and this is what you should obey. The process is to behave as you would with normal packing but leave the start of each part with the correct offset and the end as well respecting the real stride the block will have. Gebp is aware of both blocks stride and offset and behaves accordingly. \Hypertarget{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_aa790fec03f0d142eaadf355b13b1076d_aa790fec03f0d142eaadf355b13b1076d}\index{Eigen::internal@{Eigen::internal}!storeComplexAccumulator@{storeComplexAccumulator}}

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{tridiagonalization\_inplace()}{tridiagonalization\_inplace()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespace_eigen_1_1internal_af990ea26c76604813634bbbe753147d7_af990ea26c76604813634bbbe753147d7} 
template$<$typename \mbox{\hyperlink{benchmark-blocking-sizes_8cpp_af5fcaa2ea9f565466ca96c2992ea0771_af5fcaa2ea9f565466ca96c2992ea0771}{Matrix\+Type}} , typename Diagonal\+Type , typename Sub\+Diagonal\+Type , typename Coeff\+Vector\+Type $>$ \\
\mbox{\hyperlink{_macros_8h_a9efec3cfd22b9a33bead9c6718d128da_a9efec3cfd22b9a33bead9c6718d128da}{EIGEN\+\_\+\+DEVICE\+\_\+\+FUNC}} void Eigen\+::internal\+::tridiagonalization\+\_\+inplace (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{benchmark-blocking-sizes_8cpp_af5fcaa2ea9f565466ca96c2992ea0771_af5fcaa2ea9f565466ca96c2992ea0771}{Matrix\+Type}} \&}]{mat}{, }\item[{Diagonal\+Type \&}]{diag}{, }\item[{Sub\+Diagonal\+Type \&}]{subdiag}{, }\item[{Coeff\+Vector\+Type \&}]{hcoeffs}{, }\item[{bool}]{extractQ}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



Performs a full tridiagonalization in place 


\begin{DoxyParams}[1]{引数}
\mbox{\texttt{ in,out}}  & {\em mat} & On input, the selfadjoint matrix whose tridiagonal decomposition is to be computed. Only the lower triangular part referenced. The rest is left unchanged. On output, the orthogonal matrix Q in the decomposition if {\ttfamily extractQ} is true. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em diag} & The diagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T in the decomposition. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ out}}  & {\em subdiag} & The subdiagonal of the tridiagonal matrix T in the decomposition. \\
\hline
\mbox{\texttt{ in}}  & {\em extractQ} & If true, the orthogonal matrix Q in the decomposition is computed and stored in {\ttfamily mat}.\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}
Computes the tridiagonal decomposition of the selfadjoint matrix {\ttfamily mat} in place such that $ mat = Q T Q^* $ where $ Q $ is unitary and $ T $ a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix.

The tridiagonal matrix T is passed to the output parameters {\ttfamily diag} and {\ttfamily subdiag}. If {\ttfamily extractQ} is true, then the orthogonal matrix Q is passed to {\ttfamily mat}. Otherwise the lower part of the matrix {\ttfamily mat} is destroyed.

The vectors {\ttfamily diag} and {\ttfamily subdiag} are not resized. The function assumes that they are already of the correct size. The length of the vector {\ttfamily diag} should equal the number of rows in {\ttfamily mat}, and the length of the vector {\ttfamily subdiag} should be one left.

This implementation contains an optimized path for 3-\/by-\/3 matrices which is especially useful for plane fitting.

\begin{DoxyNote}{覚え書き}
Currently, it requires two temporary vectors to hold the intermediate Householder coefficients, and to reconstruct the matrix Q from the Householder reflectors.
\end{DoxyNote}
